name: CyberPower CP1500PFCLCD UPS
comments: There have been a lot of intense storms in my area this summer and the power went out in my apartment building 5 times in a month (including twice since I built my PC, so the UPS has already been incredibly useful). This was a very necessary purchase, no complaints here
Not spending a ton of money on a computer to not keep it protected works great and I can see how much I draw very good UPS.
Wanted to stabilize the power since I have a big PSU and this for the bill nicely.
whiny
It has saved my work from deletion a few times over now, and it's right at the stopping point in the market before prices skyrocket.

Of all the UPSs that I have tried, this is the one that worked best for me, I have not had to change batteries, it shows me the energy consumption on the computer and it takes great care of me in the face of energy changes that we normally and habitually suffer in the Dominican Republic.

I love this thing and the monitoring software is simple and easy to use. It's great value for a 1500VA 1000W and Power Factor Correction (PFC) UPS. What I will say though, if you have a power supply for your PC that is half decent or from any decently-known name, you don't need to pay for the PFC version, get the CP1500AVRLCD which is the same thing with a simulated sine wave output instead and save the $20-$40. If you needed the PFC aspect, you would know that you would need it because of the special electronics you'd be plugging in.

I love this UPS! My area gets a lot of random power outages for some reason, and I sadly learned the hard way after frying my last CPU that I need a UPS :'( which still confused me because even without the UPS, I had my PC connected to a surge protector. But I guess it wasn't working...
Anyways, this UPS works great and has awesome 1000W capacity to power my gaming rig. It also has an LCD screen on it which is super convenient to see current battery level, current load, etc. Also the software is easy to set up and use. I set it up to shut the PC down safely immediate when a power loss is detected.

Solid UPS for an area with brown power and lines that frequently go down to storms. Supporting an EVGA 1000w G2 + Ryzen 5950x + 3080Ti FTW3 build with 2 monitors. Gives me plenty of time to shut down in case of an outage.
Working very well so far, painless setup.

name: APC Back-UPS 1500 UPS
comments:
I use this as a redundecy for the PC. Works well and I plan on putting my wifi and a server on this in the future.
I has a light on at all times and everything is analog buttons. There is a screen that helps too. It beeps real loud too let you know its using its own battery.

Great UPS. If the battery dies don't bother buying one from APC. I sat back ordered for over a year without a replacement. I ended up ordering a generic on Amazon and its been working great. In fact the generic on Amazon is what the company ended up referring me to purchase.

The unit I have has given me no issues, which I can honestly say has surprised me, and it has saved my PC twice. I've replaced the battery twice, once because of a power surge and once because of battery age, and both replacements were easy. I got my batteries from B&H.

The unit worked well... for a week. After that, I was getting F01/F02 errors every other time I tried to turn my computer on. Restarting the unit would work... for about a day before the errors would come up again. After three times, I gave up: since F02s indicate actual physically blown fuses, and since I'm working near potentially-flammable items and carpet, I decided it wasn't worth the risk and refunded the unit. The repeated start-stops when the unit fuses blew probably damaged my computer's components far more than had I just been using the wall outlet... Maybe I just got unlucky, but given this is my first experience with APC, I was extremely disappointed. I'll just be using a standard surge protector from now on.
Marked $0.00 because it was refunded.
Didn't expect anything less

What's the point of spending a ton of money on a really good computer build if you're not going to protect it from a power surge? I went way overboard with this but I really wanted something that would handle electrical anomalies with ease and reliable protection. I can run 2 monitors, my rig, a space heater, and my printer for an extended 1hr to 1hr 30mins after my power goes out. I know I won't be able to have internet but if I were to hook my router and modem into this thing, I could still potentially run for a bit with electricity. Def a nice to have item and not a must have though.
My town’s electricity is **** so this is a must have

name: APC Back-UPS Pro 1500S UPS
comments:
We get only 2 or 3 power failures a year but that is too many for me to lose all connectivity in my home.
I connected my router, modem, IP Phone, PiHoles (2), and critical switches and my Mother Ship computer.
When the power fails it alerts me by text and email before it shuts down the Mother Ship https://pcpartpicker.com/b/xFGqqs It also sets up a countdown timer showing how long the network will stay functional which is generally 172 minutes.
It also smooths out the power to everything connected to the regulated outlets.
This thing is priceless for its functionality.
When you need protection.

performed well as expected, had no issues so far. one of the most vital important but underrated PC component. My friend literally told me to invest in a good reputable UPS in order to protect all the PC components from potential outage or power surge, abnormal voltages...
Quoted "The UPS is also a surge protector that protects connected devices from power problems, like surges or abnormal voltages, which can damage, reduce lifespan, or affect performance of electronic equipment and devices."

name: CyberPower CP1000PFCLCD UPS
comments: Been a few times now my house has had a brown out or black out and this bad boy definitely saved me while I was working. Any interruption in power and you hear it power on instantly.

I previously purchased a simulated sinewave 850v and it lasted 2 minutes when at 25% load. After some research, I figured out the problem and purchased a replacement. Go with a true sinewave.
Update - Even this bigger sine wave UPS won't live up to the advertised runtime. At 100 watts I'd be lucky to get 15 minutes out of it.

After several weeks of having this ups I am glad I have it. The power here goes out for a few seconds sometimes, especially during storms. I never even think about or see the ups until I hear that click that means it's running on battery power. I don't do a lot of important work, but it is nice to not have to restart my computer and wait for my router to come back online when the power blinks out.
I have a 500w power supply and was a little worried about only getting the 1000VA/600w model, but looking at the screen I only use around 100 watts under normal use, and even when stress testing the cpu (Ryzen 5 1500x) and gpu (GTX 1060 6GB), it doesn't go much over 200 watts. I have my modem/router, pc, and monitor all plugged into the battery side, and this is one of the few times that I've been happy I didn't spend extra for a more powerful unit.

A fantastic choice of UPS! It's a Line Interactive type, which means that it will power your PC off of mains power directly, avoiding the battery altogether unless there is a blackout or brownout, and it compensates for inconsistent mains power by automatically correcting undervoltages or overvoltages. It also has something called "Pure Sine Wave" technology, which is just a fancy way of saying that it's digital DC-to-AC transformer is good enough to fool a high-end "Active PFC" PC power supply into thinking it's getting "authentic" AC.
Runs out of the box, but also includes a USB hookup and pleasant monitoring software (that stays quiet when you aren't looking for it) if you want to monitor your UPS more directly. The monitoring software cheekily integrates with both Ubuntu and Windows 10, providing battery charge levels to the OS as if the whole computer were a laptop!
Buy one if you're considering one and you won't regret the purchase.

name: CyberPower CP1300EPFCLCD UPS
comments:
It gets the job done. In Australia, CyberPower units are usually the cheapest for around $250-$400 AUD for 1000-1300VA units.
However, there was a video circulating on Reddit of a unit catching fire if you unplug and re-plug it into the wall during use. It was blamed on some QA issues with some flammable glue(??). I have emailed CyberPower for comment and they have said that it is due to improper grounding. You are not supposed to unplug it from the wall, even when the wall switch is off (and therefore, ungrounding the unit) and plug it back in (reintroducing the ground connection) as it can catch fire. Scary. A reminder to never mess around with these things otherwise they will explode in your face. Only unplug UPSs while the unit itself is switched off.
Mine hasn't caught fire yet, so, 5 stars for now!

comments: After I had a few power outages, I decided to invest in this machine and so far I'm happy with it. It runs for about 20 minutes with everything on.

I really think people underestimate the usefulness of an UPS. I have had 3 power outages this summer and this thing has worked flawlessly. One time I didn't even realize the power went out until I got booted from game for network issues. It allows me plenty of time to shutdown my computer properly and the front facing USB ports are nice for charging phones or tablets in an emergency situation.
It's running great. Nice to have an UPS incase the power goes out. CyberPower makes great UPSs and the software is nice to monitor and tweak the settings.
My second CyberPower UPS (the first is still in use), and not disappointed. Easily supports the full system plus other peripherals (modem, router, etc.).

Power outages and brownouts are fairly common where I live, and the wiring in my house is not great, hence why I decided to buy a UPS. This particular model is designed to work with active PFC power supplies (which is not supposed to strain the PSU when it goes into batter backup mode), which is why I chose to go with this one over some of the cheaper models that only offered simulated sine wave. It's already saved me from a few outages in the month that I've had it, so it's doing it's job pretty well, so far. My only gripe is that the software looks extremely outdated, but that's a small con.

comments: Great ups
I get power outages from time to time and this baby will keep my fancy rig from frying.

Fits my needs well. It will give me ample time to shut my rig down during a power outage (around 35 - 40 minutes), and then give me some extra time to help charge my phone or run a little lamp. It has a very good amount of power ports, a usb-c, usb port, and a nice little display. It's an investment protection; some added insurance and peace of mind. I didn't want to drop months of hard earned savings just to have it fried out a week later to a power surge or volt drop. It was worth the extra couple weeks of waiting.

This UPS works well. Gives me plenty of time to shut down my system, and with the remaining battery charge, was able to recharge multiple phones many times, and use my USB lamp during a 24 hour power outage. And it still had half it's battery left at the end of the power outage!
Does it's job. so far' it's saved my pc from about 2 hours worth of power outages, over the last 3 years.
A++ I wouldn't have a pc without one
Great. --more then that. When my power went out I was able to blast music off of my computer for hours, and many of which, I had my windows down.

It's a chonky boy and it has a decent amount of battery. My rig has a 650W PSU and having that and my laptop plugged in, the display estimates an hour of battery life. With everything off, it estimates 8 hours. There's software available too. It works straight out of the box after plugging it into the wall; it holds a nearly full charge on arrival.

BIG, BEEFY BOY. It's expensive, it weighs about half a million pounds, but you will not regret having it. Power flickers and outages are nothing for it. It will power all but the most excessive systems for upwards of an hour - even longer in most cases. Something I find rather nice is all the readouts it gives you; I've used this thing to test my rig's maximum power draw, which actually came out to about 414W.
Overall, worth the money!
Piece of mind and does the job.
